claims.quote: If symptoms suggest cauda equina syndrome, MRI should be done immediately if available. If MRI is unavailable, CT myelography should be done.

claims.text: Cauda equina syndrome = ⍉a spinal cord syndrome, but it mimics conus medullaris syndrome, causing similar Sx
claims.quote: Cauda equina syndrome is not a spinal cord syndrome. However, it mimics conus medullaris syndrome, causing similar symptoms.

claims.text: Unlike subacut or chronic spinal cord inj, musc tone and deep tendon reflexes are ↓in the legs; a severe acute cord inj can initially decrease or abolish them too (spinal shock), making the two hard to distinguish soon after inj
claims.quote: In cauda equina syndrome (unlike in subacute or chronic spinal cord injury), muscle tone and deep tendon reflexes are decreased in the legs. However, if an acute spinal cord injury is severe, muscle tone and deep tendon reflexes are initially decreased or absent (spinal shock), making distinguishing it from cauda equina syndrome difficult soon after injury.

claims.text: Eti Mech: 2 or more of the 18 n. roots caudal to the conus medullaris are compressed or damaged, disrupting motor and sensory pathways to the lower extremities and bladder
claims.quote: Cauda equina syndrome occurs when 2 or more of the 18 nerve roots caudal to the conus medullaris are compressed or damaged, disrupting motor and sensory pathways to the lower extremities and bladder.

claims.text: Most commonly a herniated disc in the lumbar spine; others incl congenital anomalies (eg, spina bifida), spinal cord infect, spinal epidural abscess, spinal cord tumor, spinal cord trauma, spinal stenosis (rarely), arteriovenous malformation and comp after spinal surg; many of these cause swelling that contributes to n. compress
claims.quote: Cauda equina syndrome most commonly results from a herniated disc in the lumbar spine. Other causes include congenital neurologic anomalies (eg, spina bifida), spinal cord infection, spinal epidural abscess, spinal cord tumor, spinal cord trauma, spinal stenosis (rarely), arteriovenous malformation, and complications after spinal surgery. Many of these conditions cause swelling, which contributes to compression of the nerves.

claims.text: Sx Bilat leg weakness in muscles supplied by L3 thru S1, sensory loss in the affected roots' distribution (often the saddle area), and bladder, bowel and pudendal dysfun (eg, urinary retention, urinary freq, urinary or fecal incont, erectile dysfun, loss of rectal tone, abnorm bulbocavernosus and anal wink reflexes)
claims.quote: Cauda equina syndrome (like conus medullaris syndrome) causes bilateral leg weakness in muscles supplied by L3 through S1 and sensory loss in the distribution of the affected nerve roots (often in the saddle area), as well as bladder, bowel, and pudendal dysfunction (eg, urinary retention, urinary frequency, urinary or fecal incontinence, erectile dysfunction, loss of rectal tone, abnormal bulbocavernosus and anal wink reflexes).

claims.text: W.o tx, cauda equina syndrome can cause complete paralysis of the lower extremities
claims.quote: Without treatment, cauda equina syndrome can cause complete paralysis of the lower extremities.

claims.quote: If cauda equina syndrome is causing sphincter dysfunction (eg, causing urine retention or incontinence) and/or lower extremity weakness, immediate surgery (eg, discectomy, laminectomy) is required.

claims.text: Analgesics prn; if nonopioid analgesics do ⍉relieve Sx, corticosteroids can be given systemically or as an epidural inj, though analgesia tends to be modest and temp; corticosteroids can also reduce swelling
claims.quote: Analgesics should be used as needed to relieve pain. If symptoms are not relieved with nonopioid analgesics, corticosteroids can be given systemically or as an epidural injection; however, analgesia tends to be modest and temporary. Corticosteroids can also reduce swelling.

claims.text: Pts w Sx of cauda equina syndrome (eg, LE weakness as well as urinary retention, freq or incont) require immediate surg decompression
claims.quote: Patients with symptoms of cauda equina syndrome (eg, lower extremity weakness as well as urinary retention, frequency, or incontinence) require immediate surgical decompression.
